headline: Microsoft turns to AWS as GitHub faces AI capacity crunch
summary: GitHub's AI-driven usage has strained Microsoft's Azure infrastructure, leading the company to seek additional cloud capacity from Amazon Web Services to meet demand.
details: Microsoft is reportedly adding Amazon Web Services (AWS) capacity for GitHub. This move comes as AI-driven usage has significantly strained the developer platform, exposing the limitations of Microsoft's own Azure infrastructure.

The surge in demand is largely attributed to AI features, such as GitHub Copilot, which require substantial computational resources. This highlights the escalating infrastructure costs associated with agentic coding and advanced AI applications.

By leveraging AWS, Microsoft aims to ensure GitHub can continue to scale and meet the growing needs of its developer community. This cross-cloud strategy underscores the intense competition and specialized capabilities within the cloud computing market.
caption:
Microsoft is turning to its rival, Amazon Web Services, to handle the growing AI demands of GitHub.

Microsoft is reportedly adding Amazon Web Services (AWS) capacity for GitHub. This move comes as AI-driven usage has significantly strained the developer platform, exposing the limitations of Microsoft's own Azure infrastructure.

The surge in demand is largely attributed to AI features, such as GitHub Copilot, which require substantial computational resources. This highlights the escalating infrastructure costs associated with agentic coding and advanced AI applications.

By leveraging AWS, Microsoft aims to ensure GitHub can continue to scale and meet the growing needs of its developer community. This cross-cloud strategy underscores the intense competition and specialized capabilities within the cloud computing market.
